items.description: UBOS findings show that nearly nine in 10 household water samples contained E. coli, exposing a major gap between access to improved water sources and the safety of water consumed.
items.author: Muhamadi Matovu
items.excerpt: Only 15.1 per cent of Ugandans have access to safely managed drinking water, despite 81.4 per cent using improved water sources, according to new findings by the Uganda Bureau of Statistics (UBOS). The assessment also found widespread faecal contamination, with 88.9 per cent of drinking water samples collected from households containing E. coli, bacteria commonly found in the intestines of humans and animals. The presence of E. coli in drinking water indicates possible faecal contamination and the risk of exposure to disease-causing microorganisms that can cause diarrhoea and other illnesses.
